title: Using OSS models to build AI apps with millions of users — Hassan El Mghari
talk_summary: A DevRel engineer at Together AI demos ~40 small open-source AI apps he built (image gen, commit-message writer, text-to-app) and describes his repeatable process: keep an idea list, build the simplest possible version with one or two API calls, polish the UI heavily, launch early, and swap in newer models as they ship.

takeaways.technique: One-line model swap to upgrade existing apps
takeaways.what_they_do: Keeps model choice as a thin, replaceable layer so a newer/better model can be dropped into an existing app with a minimal change, and re-launches the app on the new model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of the time it's like a oneline change of like let me update this model and the app just gets way better

takeaways.technique: Radical simplicity — one or two API calls per feature
takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately designs each app around a single model call and a single endpoint rather than multi-step pipelines, to move fast and validate cheaply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of my apps have only one or two API calls

takeaways.what_they_do: Keeps a running list of ideas with a standing top-five, so when a new model or opportunity appears he can immediately pick the next build instead of stalling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I usually always have this short list of like the top five

takeaways.technique: Launch early, iterate on real usage
takeaways.what_they_do: Ships the smallest working version in about a week and only invests further once real users respond, rather than building a grandiose version for months.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you didn't spend 6 months building, you spent a week building and you can kind of move on

takeaways.what_they_do: Because apps are open source, he asks infra vendors (DB, auth, inference) for free credits and they usually grant them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you launch something and you reach out to these companies ... More often than not, they will
